en.html:
The observation room, at the very stern.
A grand view to enjoy. Within limits, haan—military vessel, not pleasure boat. Glass on every side was a luxury it could not afford.

Apart from the view, nothing to see. No suspicious object.
Only one way in or out, too.

en.html:
No answer. Kanae went over, stopped just short of the place she was watching, and crouched.

I followed and came around opposite her.
Sayo Nagakura needed no explanation. Already beside the doorway, watching outside. Some people’s understanding did not need to be dragged along by the hand.

Kageaki"Then, Captain—"

No—there was a hidden door in the floor.
And we had the key borrowed from the captain.

I put it into the small keyhole, praying without deciding who was supposed to receive the prayer.
If this was the wrong key... probably finished. Time to search for another, we did not have.

Very few words. Enough understanding.

—After coming this far, I was not going to stand here cultivating hesitation.

I took the stairs first. Captain Ootori followed. Last came the old attendant, like a shadow.

Footsteps quiet, down to the lower level..................
